selection.population: all friends-of-friends haloes above 1e8 Msun that hold stars (each halo counts once, with all stars inside r200)
selection.warning: Galaxy stellar mass function of the whole CoDa II box at z = 6, counted by sim-highline from the public catalogue (0.25 dex bins; error bars are Poisson). A galaxy is a friends-of-friends halo, so the satellites of a halo are inside its stellar mass; only haloes above 1e8 Msun (246 particles) are in the catalogue, and bins are kept only where at least 10 galaxies are counted and no more than 1 percent of them live in haloes below 2e8 Msun, so that the missing lighter haloes cannot change the bin (the lowest kept bin is log M* = 5.125). The box is a constrained realization of the Local Universe, not a random volume. The paper states the Kroupa IMF only for its ionizing and UV source model, so the IMF of the stellar mass is left unspecified.

selection.warning: Median stellar-to-halo mass ratio of the whole CoDa II box at z = 6, computed by sim-highline from the public catalogue in 0.25 dex bins of halo mass; haloes without stars count as a ratio of zero, so a bin is kept only where more than half of its haloes hold stars (the lightest kept bin is log Mh = 9.125; below it the median is zero because star formation is suppressed or has not started) and holds at least 10 haloes; the 16th percentile is given only where it is above zero. The halo mass is the friends-of-friends mass and the stellar mass is all stars inside r200, satellites included. The box is a constrained realization of the Local Universe, not a random volume.
